text:
Please draw a new pose sheet showing only the SPIN part of Sora's ground grab in our 2D fighting game.




Attached: (1) Sora's battle idle, rendered from his own 3D model - his look, outfit and Kingdom Key; (2) an earlier concept sheet of the whole grab. Keep its style, its pose 1 (the grab) and its pose 4 (the toss). Its poses 2 and 3 were wrong: the opponent stayed on Sora's right the whole time instead of being swung around him.




The opponent is a second Sora. In every pose Sora's LEFT hand keeps hold of the opponent's jacket at the chest, arm stretched out straight by the pull; the Kingdom Key stays in his RIGHT hand, held low and close to his body.




Sora turns ONE full circle on the spot, and the opponent is dragged around him in a wide circle, feet OFF the floor, body leaning far out and nearly horizontal from the force:

1. Start (same as the earlier pose 1): Sora facing screen right, the opponent in front of him on the RIGHT, feet still on the floor.

2. Quarter turn: Sora pivots to face the viewer; the opponent is swung round to the FRONT of him (closest to the viewer), lifted off the floor, legs trailing.

3. Half turn: Sora faces screen LEFT; the opponent flies on his LEFT side, stretched out almost horizontal at waist-to-chest height.

4. Three-quarter turn: Sora's back is to the viewer; the opponent is behind him (furthest from the viewer), partly hidden by Sora's body, legs flying out.

5. Full turn: Sora faces screen right again, the opponent swung back round to the RIGHT, still off the floor - the moment just before the toss.

6. Toss (same as the earlier pose 4): Sora heaves the opponent up into the air in front of him on the right.




Rules: Sora's feet stay on the same floor line, same scale in every pose, knees bend naturally; only his LEFT hand ever touches the opponent; the Keyblade never leaves his right hand and keeps the same length.




Image: 6 poses in two rows of three, plain white background, same 2D cel style, no text.
